# MS Access Form to ASP.NET Core Conversion

> **FPSAPPS** is the overall system. Backend API projects: `Apha.FPS`, `Apha.PACT`, `Apha.Costbook`, `Apha.PIMS`. Frontend: `Apha.FPSApps`.
>
> | Placeholder | Description | Example |
> |---|---|---|
> | `[App]` | App module supplied as the first prompt argument (PascalCase) | `FPS`, `PACT`, `Costbook`, `PIMS` |
> | `[FormName]` | Form name supplied as the second prompt argument (PascalCase, no spaces) | `StaffJob`, `MonthlyOutputLog` |
> | `[Entity]` | Primary database table/entity derived from the `.frm` RecordSource | `StaffJob` |
> | `[EntityView]` | Read-only view entity derived from the `.frm` RecordSource query | `StaffJobView` |
> | `[KeyType]` | Primary key C# type derived from the entity | `int`, `string`, `Guid` |
> | `[KeyName]` | Primary key property name | `StaffJobId` |

## Quick Start — How to Run This Prompt

> ⚠️ **This prompt requires VS Code, not Visual Studio.**  
> The `/` slash-command autocomplete, `argument-hint` display, and `agent` mode
> are VS Code Copilot Chat features only — they are not available in Visual Studio
> (devenv.exe). If you are currently in Visual Studio, open this workspace in
> VS Code before continuing.

**Step 1 — Open VS Code** (not Visual Studio) with the FPSAPPS workspace folder open, then open the **GitHub Copilot Chat** panel (`Ctrl+Alt+I`).

**Step 2 — Make sure you are in Agent mode** — the mode selector at the bottom of the chat input must show **Agent**, not Ask or Edit. If it shows Ask or Edit, click it and select **Agent**. This prompt reads source files, analyses VBA, and writes output files — it requires full tool access.

**Step 3 — Confirm source files are in place** before running:

| Required file | Location |
|---|---|
| MS Access form definition | `source/frm/[App]/[FormName].frm` |
| Subform definition(s) *(if the main `.frm` contains `Begin Subform` blocks)* | `source/frm/[App]/fsub[SubformName].frm` — one file per subform; the name comes from `SourceObject = "Form.fsubXxx"` in the main `.frm` |

For the HTML prototype, **check `source/ui/[App]/` and determine which pattern is present**:

| Pattern | When present | Files to read |
|---|---|---|
| **Single-file** | One file named exactly `[FormName].html` | `source/ui/[App]/[FormName].html` only |
| **Multi-file** | Files named `[FormName]-add.html` / `[FormName]-edit.html` (and optionally `[FormName]-delete.html`) | All present `-add`, `-edit`, `-delete` files |

> If neither pattern is found the agent must stop and report the missing HTML prototype.

Additionally, check whether the following **optional** artefacts exist and read each one that is referenced by the `.frm`:

| Optional artefact | Location | Contains |
|---|---|---|
| MS Access named queries | `source/msaccessqry/[App]/[QueryName].msaccsql` | Parameterised SELECT / ACTION queries |
| SQL Server stored procedures | `source/mssql/[DbName]/Procedures/[SpName].sql` | Business logic invoked via VBA `CreateQueryDef` blocks |
| SQL Server functions | `source/mssql/[DbName]/functions/[FunctionName].sql` | Scalar or table-valued functions used in SQL strings |
| SQL Server triggers | `source/mssql/[DbName]/triggers/[TriggerName].sql` | DML triggers on tables the form writes to |
| PostgreSQL views | `source/pgsql/[schema]/Views/[viewname].sql` (fallback: `source/mssql/[DbName]/views/[ViewName].sql`) | Views used as `RecordSource` or `RowSource` |
| PostgreSQL tables | `source/pgsql/[schema]/Tables/[tablename].sql` (fallback: `source/mssql/[DbName]/Tables/[TableName].sql`) | Authoritative column names, types, PKs, and FKs for entity generation |
| VBA BAS module | `source/bas/[App]/[ModuleName].bas` | Shared VBA functions called by the `.frm` that are not defined inside it |

**`[DbName]`** is determined by the app:

| App | DbName(s) |
|---|---|
| `FPS` | `fps` |
| `PACT` | `fps` |
| `Costbook` | `fps`, `mabarchive` |
| `PIMS` | `mabarchive` |

> The agent will stop with an error if the two required files are missing. Optional artefacts are read **only when referenced by the `.frm`** — do not read the entire folder.

**Step 4 — Type the slash command** in the chat input, selecting this prompt from the `/` menu, then append the app name and form name:

| What you want to convert | Command to type |
|---|---|
| FPS — StaffJob form | `/Access Form to ASP.NET Core FPS StaffJob` |
| PACT — MonthlyOutputLog form | `/Access Form to ASP.NET Core PACT MonthlyOutputLog` |
| Costbook — RateCard form | `/Access Form to ASP.NET Core Costbook RateCard` |
| PIMS — ProjectSelection form | `/Access Form to ASP.NET Core PIMS ProjectSelection` |

Valid app names (PascalCase): **`FPS`  `PACT`  `Costbook`  `PIMS`**

**Step 5 — Wait.** The agent reads both source files in full, then works through each phase in order — writing all output files directly into the workspace. No further input is needed unless a stop response is shown.

## Purpose

Convert a Microsoft Access Form into a full end-to-end ASP.NET Core solution following the established clean architecture, naming conventions, and patterns already in place.

---

## Concurrency Lock (FIRST THING TO DO — before any other step)

The agent uses a single lock file `zPostRunValidationArtefacts/.codingagent-lock` to prevent two conversion runs from executing simultaneously in the same workspace folder. A phase history table inside the lock file tracks every phase that has run.

### Lock file format

```
agent-name: Access Form to ASP.NET Core
form-name: <[App] [FormName] — as supplied in the prompt argument>
current-phase: <name of the phase currently executing>
started: <ACTUAL machine timestamp — ISO-8601 format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss>

| Phase                   | Start               | Status      | End                 | Reason                          |
|-------------------------|---------------------|-------------|---------------------|---------------------------------|
| <<current phase>>       | <ACTUAL timestamp>  | IN-PROGRESS |                     |                                 |
```

> **Timestamps must be real.** Always obtain the current machine time by running `Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss'` in the terminal. **Never** hardcode or reuse example timestamps. Every `Start` and `End` value in the phase history table must reflect the actual time the phase began or ended.
> **Reason** — leave blank for `IN-PROGRESS` and `COMPLETED`; populate with a short failure description when `Status = FAILED`.

### On startup — check for an existing lock

1. Use `file_search` to check whether `zPostRunValidationArtefacts/.codingagent-lock` exists.
2. **If the file exists**, read it and then **immediately stop** with this message to the user:

   ```
   ❌ A conversion session is already running.
   Agent:         Access Form to ASP.NET Core
   Form:          <form-name value>
   Current phase: <current-phase value>
   Started at:    <started value>
   Please wait for that session to complete, or archive the stale lock by renaming
   zPostRunValidationArtefacts/.codingagent-lock
   to
   zPostRunValidationArtefacts/codingagentrun_<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss>.log
   ```

   **Do not proceed past this point.**

3. **If the file does not exist**, ensure the `zPostRunValidationArtefacts/` folder exists (create it if it does not). Then create `zPostRunValidationArtefacts/.codingagent-lock` with the format above, inserting the first phase row as `IN-PROGRESS`.

4. **Reset file ACLs on the `src/` folder** — run this once before writing any files. Pre-existing files cloned from a network share, OneDrive, or a zip archive can carry restrictive ACLs (`BUILTIN\Users:(I)(RX)` — read/execute only) that will cause "Insufficient permissions" or "Failed to save … Insufficient permissions. Select 'Retry as Admin'" errors mid-run.

   Run **both commands** in order from the workspace root:

   ```powershell
   # Step 1 — reset all file-level ACL overrides so files inherit from their parent folder
   icacls "src" /reset /T /C /Q

   # Step 2 — explicitly grant the current user Modify rights on every file and subfolder
   icacls "src" /grant "${env:USERNAME}:(OI)(CI)M" /T /C /Q
   ```

   Then **verify write access** is effective before proceeding:

   ```powershell
   $testFile = "src\.acl-writecheck"
   [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText((Resolve-Path "src").Path + "\.acl-writecheck", "ok")
   if (Test-Path $testFile) { Remove-Item $testFile; Write-Host "ACL OK — write access confirmed" }
   else { Write-Host "ACL FAILED — do not proceed; ask the user to run VS Code as Administrator" }
   ```

   > **Why two steps?** `/reset` removes file-level overrides and reverts files to inherit from their parent. But if the parent folder itself carries restrictive permissions (e.g. from a zip extract or network share), inherited permissions are equally restrictive. The explicit `/grant` ensures the current user has `Modify` (read + write + delete) regardless of what the parent inherits. Together the two commands are idempotent — running them when permissions are already correct has no effect.
   >
   > **If the verify step prints "ACL FAILED"**: the workspace folder itself is on a read-only share or the user does not have local admin rights. Stop and instruct the user: *"Please re-open VS Code using 'Run as Administrator', or copy the workspace to a local writable folder, then re-run the prompt."* Do not attempt to write any source files until write access is confirmed.

   Errors on `bin/` or `obj/` paths can be ignored — only source files matter.

   Then continue to the "Before You Start" section below.

### During execution — keep the lock file current

- **When a phase starts:** update `current-phase` in the header and add a new row to the phase history table with `Status = IN-PROGRESS` and the actual start timestamp.
- **When a phase ends successfully:** update that row with `Status = COMPLETED` and the actual end timestamp.
- **If the agent stops due to an error:** update the row with `Status = FAILED`, the actual end timestamp, and a short failure reason in the Reason column before stopping.

### On completion (or on error) — archive the lock

Do **not** delete `.codingagent-lock`. Instead, **rename** it to preserve the full run history:

```
zPostRunValidationArtefacts/codingagentrun_<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss>.log
```

Use `Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd_HHmmss'` to obtain the timestamp. Rename the file using `Rename-Item`:

```powershell
Rename-Item `
  -Path  "zPostRunValidationArtefacts/.codingagent-lock" `
  -NewName "codingagentrun_$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd_HHmmss').log"
```

This applies on **successful completion** and on **error** (the lock row will already be marked `FAILED`). After the rename, the workspace is free for the next run.

## Before You Start

Follow the inputs and solution structure rules defined in:

> 📄 [01 — Inputs & Solution Structure](./../instructions/01-inputs-and-structure.instructions.md)

Read **all source files** following this order — the order matters:
1. HTML prototype(s) — detect which pattern is present in `source/ui/[App]/` and read accordingly:
   - **Single-file pattern** (`[FormName].html` exists): read that one file; the same layout covers all CRUD modes — no per-mode differences to reconcile; generates `Index.cshtml` only (no CRUD partials)
   - **Multi-file pattern** (`[FormName]-add.html` / `[FormName]-edit.html` exist): read all present files; differences between files reveal which fields are read-only, hidden, or absent per CRUD mode; generates `Index.cshtml` + `_AddEdit[FormName].cshtml` (+ `_Delete[FormName].cshtml` if `-delete.html` exists **and this is NOT a DataGrid form**)
     - `[FormName]-add.html` — Add/Create prototype; fields editable unless otherwise indicated
     - `[FormName]-edit.html` — Edit/Update prototype; key field typically read-only
     - `[FormName]-delete.html` — Delete confirmation prototype; all fields read-only *(only if file exists; **DataGrid forms ignore this file** — DataGrid delete uses a JS `confirm()` dialog, not a modal partial)*
2. `source/frm/[App]/[FormName].frm` — required; read every VBA `Sub`/`Function` body in full and extract the complete artefact reference list (named queries, SPs, functions, views, trigger-affected tables)
   - 2a. For each **subform** found in step 2 (every `Begin Subform` block with `SourceObject = "Form.fsubXxx"`) → read `source/frm/[App]/fsub[SubformName].frm` in full; extract `Name`, `LinkChildFields`, `LinkMasterFields`; run the same full artefact extraction pass (RecordSource, queries, SPs, functions, views, trigger-affected tables); add all discoveries to the same reference map
   - 2b. For each subform that has `DefaultView = 1` or `2` (will produce a DataGrid) → build a **Grid Operations Profile** by reading the top-level `Allow*` properties and the per-control `Enabled`/`Locked` properties from `fsub[SubformName].frm`:

     **Allow* properties — top of the form section:**

     | Property in `.frm` | Value | Meaning |
     |---|---|---|
     | `AllowAdditions` not listed | (absent) | Add **enabled** (Access default = True) |
     | `AllowAdditions = NotDefault` | explicitly changed | Add **disabled** (changed from True → False) |
     | `AllowEdits` not listed | (absent) | Edit **enabled** (Access default = True) |
     | `AllowEdits = NotDefault` | explicitly changed | Edit **disabled** (changed from True → False) |
     | `AllowDeletions` not listed | (absent) | Delete **enabled** (Access default = True) |
     | `AllowDeletions = NotDefault` | explicitly changed | Delete **disabled** (changed from True → False) |

     **Per-control editability — each `Begin TextBox`/`ComboBox`/`CheckBox` in the `Detail` section:**

     | Control has both `Enabled = NotDefault` AND `Locked = NotDefault` | → **Read-only** |
     | Control has neither `Enabled` nor `Locked` listed | → **Editable** |
     | `ControlSource` contains a formula (e.g. `=[NoTests]*[TestPrice]`) | → **Computed / always read-only** |

     Record the result as a named profile before writing any code:
     ```
     Grid Operations Profile — [SubformName]
     AllowAdd: true|false  AllowEdit: true|false  AllowDelete: true|false
     Editable fields:   [FieldA], [FieldB]
     Read-only fields:  [FieldC], [FieldD], [FieldE]
     Computed fields:   [FieldF]   (ControlSource is a formula)
     ```
     This profile drives four things: Add/Edit/Delete **button visibility** in `Index.cshtml`; **`AddFunction`/`EditFunction`/`DeleteFunction`** in `DataGridConfig`; which fields are `readonly` in the modal partial; and whether the `[HttpDelete]` controller endpoint and JS delete function are generated at all. **DataGrid forms never generate `_Delete[FormName].cshtml` or a `Delete (GET)` action** — delete is confirmed via a browser `confirm()` dialog.

     > **Output artefact — DataGrid forms only:** After recording every Grid Operations Profile, publish `zPostRunValidationArtefacts/[App]-[FormName]-DataGrid.md` containing:
     > - One section per subform DataGrid with the full named profile block (`AllowAdd`, `AllowEdit`, `AllowDelete`, editable / read-only / computed field lists)
     > - A column-level table for each subform:
     >   | Field | Editable? | Reason |
     >   |---|---|---|
     >   | `FieldA` | Yes | Neither `Enabled` nor `Locked` set |
     >   | `FieldB` | No (read-only) | Both `Enabled = NotDefault` and `Locked = NotDefault` |
     >   | `FieldC` | No (computed) | `ControlSource` is a formula |
   - 2c. **BAS module function lookup** — after extracting all artefact references from the `.frm` VBA code, collect every function/sub call that is **not defined inside the `.frm` itself** (i.e. not a `Private Sub`/`Private Function` in the same file). For each such call:
     1. Search `source/bas/[App]/[ModuleName].bas` for the matching `Function`/`Sub` definition (case-insensitive name match)
     2. If found, read the full function body
     3. Classify it:
        - **DB-interacting** — uses `DLookup`, `DCount`, `DMax`, `DMin`, `DSum`, `OpenRecordset`, `Execute`, `QueryDefs`, `db.Execute`, or any DAO/ADO call → **translate to a repository method** and wire into the service/controller chain
        - **Pure utility** — string/date/numeric manipulation only, no DB access → translate inline at the call site or to a static helper in `Apha.Common/Helpers/`
     4. If **not found** in any `.bas` file → add a `// TODO: [FunctionName]() — definition not found in source/bas/[App]/. Confirm with team.` placeholder at every call site
3. For each **MS Access query name** found in step 2 → read `source/msaccessqry/[App]/[QueryName].msaccsql`
4. For each **stored procedure name** found in step 2 → read `source/mssql/[DbName]/Procedures/[SpName].sql`
   - 4a. After reading each parent SP, scan its body for **child SP calls** (`EXECUTE sp_*` / `EXEC usp_*` / `EXECUTE usp_*`) → read each child SP file `source/mssql/[DbName]/Procedures/[ChildSpName].sql` immediately; repeat recursively until no further child SPs are found
5. For each **function name** found in step 2 → read `source/mssql/[DbName]/functions/[FunctionName].sql`
6. For each **view name** found in step 2 → read `source/pgsql/[schema]/Views/[viewname].sql`; if not found there, fall back to `source/mssql/[DbName]/views/[ViewName].sql`
7. For each **table written by the form** found in step 2 → check `source/mssql/[DbName]/triggers/` for matching trigger files using the filename patterns (`DTrig_`, `UITrig_`, `tI_`, `tU_`, `tD_`, `_ITrig`, `_UTrig`, `_DTrig`); always confirm target table and operation from the `ON [dbo].[TableName] FOR INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE` clause in the body
8. **For every writable entity** identified in steps 2–7 → before writing any `DbContext` configuration, search `dbscript/schemas/[app_schema]/04views/vtbl*.sql` for a view whose name corresponds to the Access table name (e.g. `vtbltestrequ_tm` for Access table `tblTestRequ_TM`). The view's `FROM` clause reveals the **real PostgreSQL table name** and its `SELECT` column aliases reveal the **real PostgreSQL column names**; these must be used in `entity.ToTable(…)` and `entity.Property(…).HasColumnName(…)`. Also check the column storage types (e.g. `double precision` vs `integer`) — if the storage type differs from the C# property type apply `.HasConversion<T>()` on that property.

   | `app_schema` mapping | Folder |
   |---|---|
   | FPS | `dbscript/schemas/01fps/04views/` |
   | PACT / Costbook / PIMS | `dbscript/schemas/02mabarchive/04views/` |

> Do **not** read whole folders upfront — only the specific files whose names were found in the `.frm`.

**Discovery checklist — complete before writing any code:**

| What to find | Where to look in the `.frm` | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| MS Access queries | Every `Sub`/`Function` body | `MyDB.QueryDefs("queryName")` |
| MS Access queries | Every control with `RowSourceType = "Table/Query"` | `RowSource = "queryName"` (bare name, no SELECT) |
| MS Access queries | Inline `RowSource` SQL | `FROM queryName` inside a SELECT string |
| Query parameters | Lines immediately after `QueryDefs(…)` | `myqd.Parameters("[Name]") = [Forms]![F]![Control]` |
| Stored procedures | Every `Sub`/`Function` body | `CreateQueryDef("tmp")` + `qd.sql = "usp_name '" & … & "'"` + `DoCmd.OpenQuery "tmp"` |
| SP parameters | The `qd.sql =` string value | Each `& [ControlName] &` fragment in order |
| SQL Server views | `RecordSource` / `RowSource` properties and SQL strings | Bare view name or `FROM vViewName` |
| SQL Server functions | `RecordSource` SQL strings and VBA `db.Execute` calls | `SELECT dbo.fn_X(…)` or `FROM dbo.fn_X(…)` |
| Trigger-affected tables | `RecordSource` bound to a writable table; VBA DML; SP bodies | Tables with `AllowEdits/Additions/Deletions = Yes`; `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` in VBA; then match table name to trigger filenames in `source/mssql/[DbName]/triggers/` using patterns: `DTrig_[T]`=DELETE, `UITrig_[T]`=INSERT+UPDATE, `tI_[T]`=INSERT, `tU_[T]`=UPDATE, `tD_[T]`=DELETE, `[T]_ITrig`=INSERT, `[T]_UTrig`=UPDATE, `[T]_DTrig`=DELETE; for `[XX]_LOG_*` patterns read body for `ON [dbo].[TableName]` |
| Subforms | Every `Begin Subform` block | `Name`, `SourceObject = "Form.fsubXxx"`, `LinkChildFields`, `LinkMasterFields` — read `source/frm/[App]/fsubXxx.frm` and run full artefact extraction (step 2a) |
| Grid Operations Profile | Each subform `.frm` with `DefaultView = 1` or `2` | Check top-level `Allow*` props: absent = True (enabled); `= NotDefault` = False (disabled). Check each `Detail` control: both `Enabled = NotDefault` AND `Locked = NotDefault` = read-only; neither listed = editable; formula `ControlSource` = computed/always read-only. Record as `AllowAdd / AllowEdit / AllowDelete` booleans + editable/read-only/computed field lists (step 2b) |
| BAS module functions | Every `Sub`/`Function` body — any call not defined in the `.frm` itself | Search `source/bas/[App]/*.bas`; classify as DB-interacting (→ repository method) or pure utility (→ inline / `Apha.Common`); flag missing definitions as `// TODO` (step 2c) |

## Execution Phases

Work through each phase **in order**. Complete all files for a phase before moving to the next.

---

### Phase 1 — Backend Layers (Steps 0–9)
*Other artefact analysis · Contracts · Entities · Repository interfaces · DTOs · Service layer · Data access · API controller · AutoMapper · DI*

> 📄 [02 — Backend Layers](./../instructions/02-backend-layers.instructions.md)

Deliverables:
- **Step 0** — Artefact analysis: single `.frm` pass → reference map → read only referenced artefact files from `source/msaccessqry/[App]/`, `source/mssql/[DbName]/Procedures/`, `source/mssql/[DbName]/functions/`, `source/pgsql/[schema]/Views/`, `source/mssql/[DbName]/triggers/`
- `[Entity]Req.cs`, `[Entity]Res.cs` — shared contracts
- `[Entity].cs` — Core entity for writable table
- `[ViewName]View.cs` — keyless EF entity for each SQL Server view used as `RecordSource`/`RowSource` *(mapped via `ToView()`, not re-implemented as LINQ)*
- `[Entity]View.cs` — result-shape entity for MS Access SELECT queries converted to LINQ
- `I[Entity]Repository.cs` — Core repository interface *(methods for every query, SP DML, function, and trigger-affected write)*
- `[Entity]Dto.cs`, `[EntityView]Dto.cs` — Application DTOs
- `I[FormName]Service.cs`, `[FormName]Service.cs` — Application service *(SP business guards, transactional orchestration, trigger-derived post-write logic)*
- `[Entity]Repository.cs`, updated `[App]DbContext.cs` — Data access *(Access queries → LINQ; SPs → LINQ; views → `ToView()`; scalar functions → C# helpers; TVFs → `FromSqlRaw`; triggers → appended to write methods)*
- `[FormName]Controller.cs` (API) *(endpoints for every SP-derived service method)*, updated `EntityMapper.cs`, `RequestMapper.cs`, `ServiceCollectionExtension.cs`

---

### Phase 2 — Frontend Layers (Steps 10–18)
*Frontend DTOs · API client interface · Service layer · HTTP client · AutoMapper · ViewModels · MVC controller · Razor view*

> 📄 [03 — Frontend Layers](./../instructions/03-frontend-layers.instructions.md)
>
> **DataGrid forms only** — if the Grid Operations Profile (step 2b) confirms at least one subform DataGrid, also follow:
> 📄 [03b — DataGrid Rules](./../instructions/03b-datagrid.instructions.md)
> *(Grid Item class · `Load*Grid` action · `DataGridConfig` with null-based button control · modal partial field editability · JS patterns)*

> ⚠️ **You must run this command before writing any ViewModel, View, or controller code:**
> ```powershell
> Test-Path "zPostRunValidationArtefacts/[App]-[FormName]-Frontend.md"
> ```
> - **`False`** → build the field-mapping table below, create the file, then resume coding.
> - **`True`** → open the file, verify the table is complete, then resume coding.
>
> **Do not write any output file until this command returns `True`.**
>
> ⚠️ **Field mapping table** — complete every row before writing any output file:
>
> | HTML `id` / label text | Entity field name | ViewModel property | `asp-for` value |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | (fill in from HTML prototype + entity) | (from `[Entity].cs`) | (must equal entity field name) | (must equal ViewModel property) |
>
> **All four columns must be consistent before writing any output file.** A label that says "Transfer Income" must have `asp-for="TransferIncome"` — not `asp-for="BudgetCvl"`. Do not proceed with output files until this table is complete.
>
> **Completeness check:** Count the `<input>`, `<select>`, and `<textarea>` elements in the HTML prototype. The generated View must contain exactly the same count of `asp-for` bindings (or `TODO` placeholders — see below). A number mismatch means a field was dropped.
>
> **Access `Lk_` prefix rule:** VBA lookup field names like `Lk_Status`, `Lk_Disease`, `Lk_Contract` must **never** appear in C#. Use the exact entity field name: `ProjectStatus`, `Disease`, `Contract`.
>
> **Unmapped field rule:** If a UI field in the HTML prototype has no confirmed entity/DTO property, do **not** omit it or guess a mapping. Instead:
> - In the ViewModel: add a `// TODO: [HtmlFieldId] — no entity field mapped. Confirm with team.` placeholder property
> - In the controller's `PopulateDropdownsAsync`: add a matching `// TODO` comment
> - In the View: render a disabled `<input>` with a `@* TODO *@` comment so the field is visible and the omission is explicit

Deliverables:
- Frontend `[Entity]Dto.cs`, `I[App][FormName]ApiClient.cs`, `I[FormName]Service.cs`, `[FormName]Service.cs`
- `[App][FormName]ApiClient.cs`, updated `[App]ApiClient.cs`
- `[FormName]ViewModel.cs`
- `[FormName]Controller.cs` (MVC), `Index.cshtml`
- Updated `ViewModelMapper.cs`, `ApiDtoMapper.cs`, `ServiceCollectionExtension.cs`
- **DataGrid forms only** (Grid Operations Profile confirms DataGrid):
  - `[FormName]Item.cs` — Grid Item class (Step 16b in `03b`)
  - `Load[FormName]Grid` action, `Get[FormName]GridConfigAsync`, CRUD endpoints — (Step 17b in `03b`)
  - `_AddEdit[FormName].cshtml` *(only when AllowAdd or AllowEdit: true)* — (Step 18b in `03b`)
  - **No `_Delete[FormName].cshtml` for DataGrid forms** — delete uses a JS `confirm()` dialog; only the `[HttpDelete]` controller action is generated when AllowDelete: true

## Standards Applied Throughout

All generated code must comply with:

> 📄 [04 — Code Standards, Naming Conventions & DataGrid Rules](./../instructions/04-standards-and-conventions.instructions.md)

Key areas covered in that file:

| Area | Rules |
|---|---|
| **Layer boundaries — backend** | API controllers (`Apha.[App].Api`) call **only** `I[FormName]Service` — never repositories, `DbContext`, or EF Core directly. Services call **only** repository interfaces — never `DbContext` directly except `Database.BeginTransactionAsync()` for multi-step SP operations. Dependency graph: `Controller → IService → IRepository → DbContext`. |
| **Layer boundaries — frontend** | MVC controllers (`Apha.FPSApps.Web`) inject **only** `IXxxService` interfaces — never `I[App]ApiClient`, `I[App][Entity]ApiClient`, repository interfaces, or `DbContext`. Dependency graph: `MVC Controller → IXxxService → I[App]ApiClient → HTTP`. If `PopulateDropdownsAsync` needs a second data source, inject a second `IXxxService` or add the method to the primary service — never reach for the API client aggregate. |

## Completion Check

> ⛔ **HARD GATE — follow this exact sequence. Do NOT skip or reorder steps.**
>
> The agent has previously skipped Step 2 (creating `Build.md` before building) and jumped straight to archiving the lock file without completing the mandatory artefact. This sequence is enforced. Each step is a blocking gate — the next step must not begin until the current one is done.
>
> **Mandatory pre-archive checklist** — tick every item before running Step 4:
> - [ ] Step 1 complete — file placement verified
> - [ ] Step 2 complete — `[App]-[FormName]-Build.md` file exists on disk
> - [ ] Step 3 complete — build ran and reached `0 Error(s)`
> - [ ] Step 4 complete — `Build.md` header shows `BUILD SUCCESS` with final warning count
>
> Only when all four boxes can be ticked may Step 5 (archive) proceed.

### Step 1 — File placement

Verify every file against:

> 📄 [05 — File Placement Checklist](./../instructions/05-file-placement-checklist.instructions.md)

### Step 2 — Create Build.md skeleton ⛔ DO THIS BEFORE RUNNING THE BUILD

> ⛔ **This step must be completed before Step 3.** The agent must create this file on disk and confirm it exists before issuing any `dotnet build` command. Running the build first and creating the file afterwards is a known failure pattern — do not repeat it.

Create **`zPostRunValidationArtefacts/[App]-[FormName]-Build.md`** now:

```markdown
# Build Issues — [App]-[FormName]

**Final status**: *(fill in after final build)*
**Errors**: *(fill in)* | **Warnings**: *(fill in)*

| # | Category | Severity | File | Error message | Root cause | Fix applied |
|---|----------|----------|------|---------------|------------|-------------|
```

Then verify the file exists before proceeding:

```powershell
Test-Path "zPostRunValidationArtefacts/[App]-[FormName]-Build.md"
```

Expected output: `True`. If `False`, create the file again — do not proceed to Step 3.

### Step 3 — Build verification

Only after `Build.md` exists on disk, run the build:

```powershell
# Run from: src/
dotnet build "Apha.FPS.All.sln" 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 8
```

Expected output: `Build succeeded.` with `0 Error(s)`.

If the build fails:
1. Read the full error line — it contains the file path, line number, and error code (e.g. `CS0246`, `CS0103`)
2. Fix the reported error
3. **Immediately append a row to `Build.md`** before re-running the build
4. Re-run the build command until it reports 0 errors
5. Do **not** proceed to Step 4 while any compile error remains

If the build succeeds on the first attempt with no errors, append to `Build.md`:
`— | — | — | — | No build issues | — | —`

### Step 4 — Finalise Build.md ⛔ MANDATORY BEFORE ARCHIVING

> ⛔ **Do NOT archive the lock file until this step is complete.**

Once the build reaches `0 Error(s)`, update the header of `Build.md`:

```markdown
**Final status**: BUILD SUCCESS
**Errors**: 0 | **Warnings**: <count>
```

Then verify the header is filled in by reading the file — confirm `Final status` no longer says `*(fill in after final build)*`.

> **Row rules:**
> - **Category**: `COMPILATION` | `MISSING_DEPENDENCY` | `TEST_FAILURE` | `CONFIGURATION`
> - **Severity**: `CRITICAL` (blocks build) | `MAJOR` (test failure / runtime risk) | `MINOR` (warning)
> - **File**: filename and line number (e.g. `XxxController.cs:14`)
> - **Fix applied**: the actual code or config change — not a description of the problem

### Step 5 — Archive lock file

Only after Step 4 is complete — confirm the checklist at the top of this section before proceeding.

1. Update the lock file — mark the final phase as **COMPLETED** (set Status = `COMPLETED`, set End timestamp).

2. Archive the lock file:

```powershell
Rename-Item `
  -Path  "zPostRunValidationArtefacts/.codingagent-lock" `
  -NewName "codingagentrun_$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd_HHmmss').log"
```
